beliefs.note: Optimal aperture balances spillage capture against re-radiation losses; typically square or near-square aspect ratios in the mid-range for 100MWth class towers.
Higher outlet temps improve cycle efficiency but increase re-radiation and material stress; optimum likely near the upper feasible limit before efficiency drops.
Sufficient tubes needed for heat transfer area, but too many increase pressure drop and crowding; log-scale optimum in the mid-thousands.
Insulation reduces conduction losses but adds cost; diminishing returns set in quickly; optimum is a moderate thickness.
Tube dimensions must maintain a specific wall thickness ratio for pressure containment while optimizing heat transfer; they scale together.
Very small inner diameters cause excessive pressure drop and pumping parasitics, violating c6.
Very large outer diameters crowd the aperture, violating c5 (bundle fit) and reducing effective flux capture.

trust.notes: Based on general CSP receiver physics and typical design trade-offs; specific optimum depends on heliostat field layout and cost constraints not fully detailed.
